name: GGUF Q4_K_S (4-bit K-quant, small)
quality_delta: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.62 vs 7.32 F16 (+0.30); GSM8K 70.83 vs 77.63; HellaSwag 77.33 vs 72.51; IFEval 72.79 vs 78.93; MMLU 80.26 vs 63.50; TruthfulQA 53.40 vs 54.79; unweighted mean 69.17 vs 69.47 (-0.43% AvgLoss); size 4468 MiB (-70.83%).
notes: The study's recommended balanced default and a Pareto-frontier point. Note the real danger in reading its table: MMLU and HellaSwag columns appear transposed in the extracted table rows for the 4-bit entries (Q4_0 MMLU 77.46 > F16 63.50 is implausible), so treat those two columns for 4-bit rows as unverified; the ppl/GSM8K/IFEval/mean columns are internally consistent across the paper's prose and its Table 6. That is a transcription ambiguity, not a measurement dispute. Weight-only: activations stay in FP16/BF16 at runtime, so there is no '4-bit activations with hardware support' claim to make here. ggml has bespoke dequantize+gemm kernels per type, but no accelerator has a GGUF/k-quant path in silicon; everything is dequantized on the fly. vLLM explicitly labels its GGUF support experimental and under-optimized and positions it as a memory-footprint tool (quant-vllm-gguf-doc). S = smaller metadata, slightly wider nominal size than Q4_K_M's advertised bpw, faster quantize (42.84 s vs 42.19 s - effectively tied).
